name: Battle of Mohács, Ottoman Conquest of Hungary
summary: Suleiman the Magnificent defeats and kills King Louis II of Hungary at Mohács. The Hungarian army of 25,000 faces an Ottoman force of 70,000-100,000. Louis drowns fleeing the battle; the Hungarian nobility is decimated. Within three weeks, Ottoman forces take Buda. The Hungarian kingdom splits into three: Ottoman Hungary, the Habsburg Rump Kingdom (Royal Hungary), and the semi-autonomous Principality of Transylvania under Ottoman suzerainty.

_quarry.structural_significance: Mohács permanently shifts the European balance of power; the Ottoman advance to Vienna (1529) begins; Hungary's destruction removes the main buffer between the Ottomans and central Europe; the Habsburg acquisition of the Hungarian crown through Louis II's death triggers a century of Habsburg-Valois conflict; the battle's consequences reshape central European politics until the late 17th century
